text.en:
Before a cricket match the umpire reads the rules so that every team plays fairly.
The teacher said, "A country also needs a rule book that applies to everyone from the Prime Minister to a child. It is called the Constitution."

The Constitution of India is the supreme law of the country. It lays down how the government works and the rights and duties of citizens. It came into force on 26 January 1950, which we celebrate as Republic Day. Dr B. R. Ambedkar chaired the drafting committee.
The Preamble begins with 'We, the people of India' and states the goals: justice, liberty, equality and fraternity. Fundamental rights include equality before law, freedom of speech, freedom of religion, protection against exploitation, and the right to education.
Fundamental duties include respecting the Constitution, the national flag and anthem, protecting the environment and helping each other. Rights and duties go together.
The Constitution is the supreme law of India. It came into force on 26 January 1950.
The Preamble begins with We, the people of India.
Fundamental rights include equality, freedom of speech and freedom of religion.
Fundamental duties include respecting the flag and protecting the environment.

problem.en: Why do rights come with duties?

text.en: If we claim a right, others also have the same right.
So we must respect their rights too.
A fair society needs both rights and duties.

prompt.en: A friend says the Constitution matters only to lawyers. How will you reply?

requiredIdeas.en: It protects the rights of every citizen.
It says how our government must work.

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking only experts need the Constitution.

points.en: The Constitution is the supreme law, in force from 26 January 1950.
The Preamble states the goals of justice, liberty, equality and fraternity.
